newsitem.title: USA: Taxman a hit at Disney World in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Taxman a hit at Disney World in Florida.

text.p: It was, in the words of one official, an effort "to put a more human face" -- or at least some mouse ears -- on the daunting and formidable Internal Revenue Service.

The IRS came to Walt Disney World Tuesday to offer beleaguered procrastinators last-minute guidance. And despite a light rain dozens of filers showed up, often standing in lines as long as those for the nearby Comedy Warehouse.
The effort put out by the government's most denigrated agency seemed to pay off.

"This is great," said Orlando resident Edward Sanderson, who brought a box full of receipts and tax forms with him. "I had an appointment with H & R Block but then I heard about this. I'm saving a hundred bucks."

Not quite. There was a $19 cover charge to get onto Disney's Pleasure Island, a six-acre nightclub complex on Lake Buena Vista. But the IRS agents were able to explain to Sanderson why his wife's tax bill went up even though her income did not.
Tourists and residents alike made use of the service.

"I can't believe I went on vacation and forgot about taxes," Bill Summers, of Dearpoint, Michigan, said. "I thought I'd spend the whole day trying to find a post office that still had some extension forms. Then I heard about this and took the kids to Planet Hollywood instead."

Susan Carroll, an IRS marketing expert, beamed as The Beatles "Taxman" blared from loudspeakers throughout the park. "We wanted to give people some extra tax help," she said. "But yes, it's also a way to put a more human face on the IRS."

IRS agents came on duty at 6 p.m. EDT, laptop computers fully charged for optional electronic filing. They stayed until midnight, the cutoff time for postal workers accompanying them to accept returns.
